source.id: TITLE:Gradient-based learning applied to document recognition
source.title: Gradient-based learning applied to document recognition

record.file_problem: The supplied text is heavily garbled, and it is cut off at 400,000 characters. The recognizable content is the named paper, but portions cannot be read reliably.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports image-classification test-error comparisons between fully connected and convolutional networks, bearing directly on V3, an original-source version.
record.gate_note: The benchmark table reports test-error values for fully connected networks and convolutional models. No random-label memorization experiment is reported in the readable text.
record.test_reason: The study is an original source for V3 and reports its own MNIST comparisons of convolutional and fully connected networks. Verdict labels are withheld because it is an original source for this version.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate but narrow: the authors report lower MNIST test errors for convolutional networks than for the tested fully connected networks, and conclude that learned features and globally trained graph-transformer systems improve document recognition.
record.recipe_differences: The paper is the named original source for the LeCun 1998 comparison; the readable benchmark lists test error rates.
record.method_sensitivity: The table distinguishes models marked [dist] and an input-size condition for LeNet−1.

fits_no_version.finding: LeNet-4's local-learning and nearest-neighbor output-layer replacements retain its 1.1% raw test error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Alternative classifiers on learned convolutional features can retain raw MNIST accuracy while improving rejection performance.

record.problems: The supplied text is garbled and truncated. Benchmark results are flattened, uncertainty is not stated, and the readable benchmark does not establish the full range of datasets and comparisons specified in V3.
record.rows_left_out: Other benchmark entries marked [dist], including fully connected models and LeNet−4 variants, are omitted because they repeat the same architecture comparison under a distinct distortion condition and the flattened listing does not permit dependable reconstruction of every model/value pairing. The comparison table is flattened in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Fitting fixed random labels and comparing their held-out performance with natural-label training.
Widening beyond a demonstrated zero-training-error threshold under the specified convergence and regularization conditions.
CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and SVHN; isolating how much advantage comes from local connectivity; learned sparse local connections; initialization from a trained convolutional network.
Adam or other adaptive optimizer comparisons with SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Large-versus-small minibatch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation measurements, their correlation with generalization gaps, and ranking against other measures.
Removing examples selected by label memorization and retraining against random-removal controls.

record.verdict_notes: The flattened Figure 9 shifts several values relative to model names; the architecture-specific prose resolves the corrections. The figure caption reports approximately 0.1 percentage-point uncertainty, contrary to the record's uncertainty-not-stated flag. Distortion-augmented comparator rows are already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not listed as missing.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and generalization on natural labels.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
The readable benchmark is on MNIST; the specified CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and SVHN settings and the trained-convolutional initialization comparison are not established in the supplied text.
